ledger.note: 1090: Hassan-i Sabbah captures Alamut without violence. 'The Alamut fortress was eventually captured from Mahdi in 1090 AD'; the Seljuk lord Mahdi was spared and paid 3,000 gold dinars. 'In the summer of 1090 AD, Hassan set out from Qazvin towards Alamut' (the Hassan-i Sabbah page: taken in 1090 after a two-year campaign; no month).
1096: the Assassins seize Rudkhan. 'The Assassins seized Persian castles of Rudkhan and Gerdkuh in 1096.' The previous holder is not named on the page; the Seljuk sultan is the reading.

region.text: Gerdkuh, about 15 km west of Damghan in the Qumis region, Semnan Province

ledger.note: 1100: Gerdkuh passes to the Nizaris. The Seljuk emir Amirdad Habashi 'acquired Gedrkuh in 1096' from Sultan Barkiyaruq; the Seljuk lieutenant and secret Isma'ili Mu'ayyad al-Din Muzaffar 'brought the fort into the Nizari Isma'ili possession in 1100'. The Order of Assassins page gives 1096.

ledger.note: 1101: the Seljuk sieges begin. 'From 1101 to 1118, attacks and sieges were made on the fortresses'; at Tabas the siege was first successful but lifted, possibly after a bribe, and the Assassins were soon re-established there.
1102: Lambsar in Assassin hands by this year. 'The estimated date of the capture of Lambsar varies between 1096 and 1102'; the later bound is used.

region.text: the Nizari fortresses attacked by the Seljuks, Tabas included

ledger.note: 1118: the Seljuk sieges end ('From 1101 to 1118'); the page records no decisive result, and Sanjar's forces struck again at Quhistan, Nishapur and Rudbar in 1126 without a decisive outcome.

ledger.counterpart: Saif al-Mulk ibn Amrun (emir of al-Kahf)
ledger.note: 1133: the Assassins buy al-Qadmus. Saif al-Mulk ibn Amrun 'recovered the fortress of al-Qadmus from the Franks' in 1132 and 'sold the fortress to the Assassins in 1133'.
1138: al-Kahf is ceded. 'the ceding of al-Kahf Castle itself to Assassin control in 1138 by Saif's son Musa in the midst of a succession struggle'.

ledger.counterpart: holder not named by the page
ledger.note: 1140: the Assassins acquire Masyaf ('the acquisition of the castle at Masyaf in 1140'); the page names no seller.

ledger.counterpart: holder not named by the page
ledger.note: 1141: the Assassins acquire Qala'at al-Khawabi, 'known to the Crusaders as La Coible, in 1141'; the page names no seller.

1157: the Assassins occupy the castle at Shaizar a second time, after the 1157 earthquake; they had earlier 'occupied the fortress at Shaizar held by the Banu Munqidh' until a local rebellion drove them out.
1158: Nur ad-Din takes the Shaizar castle, 'incorporating a castle at Shaizar that they had occupied after the 1157 earthquake into his territory' (the zengid-dynasty dossier is the receiving side).

ledger.note: 1253: the Mongols besiege Gerdkuh. Kitbuqa's forces laid siege in May 1253 (the Order of Assassins page: Kitbuqa 'began to assault several Assassin fortresses in 1253'). Hulagu's Alamut campaign of 1256 follows.

ledger.note: 1256: Alamut falls to the Mongols. The Imam Rukn al-Din Khurshah surrendered on 19 November 1256 and 'Alamut fell in December 1256'.
1256: Rudkhan's fate is on no page opened (seized 1096); it is closed with Alamut at confidence 1.
1257: Lambsar falls to the Mongols (Order of Assassins page; the Nizari Ismaili state page also gives Lambsar's fall as 1257).
1270: Baibars takes Masyaf. The Order of Assassins page: 'after taking Masyaf the year before' in its 1271 entry; its Mongol section gives 1267.

ledger.note: 1270: Gerdkuh surrenders, 'the last Nizari stronghold in Persia'. The garrison 'surrendered from want of clothing' on 15 December 1270 during Abaqa's reign after a siege begun in May 1253; the mongol-empire dossier has it held out to 1271.

notes:
A state Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names []). Five pages opened. Wikidata id not obtainable: null.
End year: the Nizari Ismaili state page's infobox ends the state in 1256 (fall of Alamut); this dossier ends it in 1273 because Gerdkuh held out to 15 December 1270 and the Syrian castles to 1273 (Order of Assassins page), and the mamluk-sultanate and ulus-of-hulegu dossiers already record gains from 'nizari-ismaili-state' in 1271 and 1256. Keyframes: a loss in year Y removes the land from year Y, except for the last two castles, which stay in the shape for 1273 and go with the dissolve event.
Disagreements between pages: Rudkhan and Gerdkuh 1096 (Order of Assassins) vs Gerdkuh 1100 (Gerdkuh page); Masyaf 1267 vs 1270; Gerdkuh surrendered December 1270 vs the mongol-empire dossier's 1271; the Order page says the Mongols ended the state 'by 1275' (a brief recapture of Alamut in 1275 is on both pages and is not drawn).
Not settled: when ar-Rusafa and al-'Ullaiqah came to the Assassins (under Sinan, 1162-1193, undated: confidence 1 at 1162); Rudkhan's fate; Quhistan (strong presence, no capture date: only Tabas 1101 is dated, and it appears as a contest zone, not as territory); Nizari influence in Aleppo (ended 1124, not territory); the Ziyarid and Sallarid lands that the infobox lists as predecessors (the ziyarid-dynasty and sallarid-dynasty dossiers attribute their ends of 1090 and about 1062 to the Nizaris; no page opened here dates a handover); tribute and protection relations in Syria (Templars, Saladin) and the 1210 recognition of the Abbasid caliph (not territory).
Gazetteer names used that it lacks: Alamut, Rudkhan, Gerdkuh, Lambsar, Qadmus, Kahf, Masyaf, Khawabi, Shaizar, Ullaiqah, Rusafa, Tabas. The Syrian ones carry country 'Syria'.
